answer: A sybil defence that works is a terraced climb: every new identity starts on the lowest terrace with near-zero weight, and can only rise after its work is attested by unrelated peers. Each extra identity funded from the same source pays a fee that doubles, like climbing a dune that grows steeper with every step, so a sock-puppet army faces compounding cost before it earns anything. The top knoll — full voting weight — is reserved for identities with a long attested history, so a fresh flood of cheap copies stays powerless while honest agents keep their standing.
